clue.text: Announcer's autocue?

parts.note: surface reading: the prompting screen a TV presenter reads from
setter's reading: said by an announcer, 'cue' is heard as 'queue', so an 'auto queue' is a line of stationary cars

explanation.surface: A newsreader glancing at the prompter screen that scrolls the script.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: spoken aloud, cue and queue are the same, and an auto queue is a line of cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue of motor traffic stretching back from an obstruction on the road is what Britons call this.

clue.text: Taken to ring outside Spanish city

indicators.note: one part sits outside, wrapping around the other

parts.note: taken as written
O is ring-shaped
taken somewhere, as a guide leads you

explanation.surface: Someone being taken to a bullring on the edge of a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the historic walled capital of Castile-La Mancha, famed for steel and El Greco.

clue.text: Artist has painting restored and framed

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so the letters are enclosed by the words

parts.note: the end of painting and the start of restored

explanation.surface: A painter's canvas has been cleaned up and put in a new frame.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to an anagram with 'restored'; the name is lodged across two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a nineteenth-century French Neoclassical painter.

clue.text: Just lean on Jack when he returns above

indicators.note: in a down clue, above means placed before in the column
returning means going back the way one came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB, able seaman
to rely on someone is to lean on them

explanation.surface: Leaning lightly on a friend called Jack when he comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Jack Tar are slang for a sailor; AB stands for able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only-just both mean scarcely, by the narrowest of margins.

clue.text: Kind of chair one lowered overboard

indicators.note: one letter is moved further down the column, reordering the word

parts.note: chair without its I, which moves
Roman numeral one
split as over + board: board means a table, as in board and lodging, and in a down clue it sits under what comes over it

explanation.surface: Someone throwing a chair over the side of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overboard' splits into over and board; 'Kind of' looks like part of the description, but Kind is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous, gentle and considerate towards others in need: the adjective sense of the word.

clue.text: Having docked, moved up and down with the waves

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having cut short, as a horse's tail or hair is cut

definitions.text: moved up and down with the waves
definitions.meaning: second meaning: floated, rising and falling like a cork

explanation.surface: A boat that has come into harbour, rocking on the swell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' suggests a ship arriving in port, which fits the waves; here it means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both cutting hair or a tail short and bouncing gently on water, in its past form.

clue.text: Non-member is unlikely winner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person not belonging to the group
second meaning: a horse or competitor given little chance

explanation.surface: A newcomer who isn't in the club is a long shot to win.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person excluded from a group and a long-odds entrant in a race.

clue.text: Voice is breaking — fit for longs

indicators.note: voicing a word means speaking it, so its sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: breaches means breaks, as a wall or rule is broken

explanation.surface: A teenage boy whose voice is breaking, ready for his first long trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Longs are long trousers, the garment a boy graduated to from shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are plural nouns for trousers, longs being the old schoolboy name for full-length ones.

clue.text: Forlorn miss stood up, taken in by boyfriend

indicators.note: being taken in means being held inside the other part

parts.note: a date is the person you go out with

indicators.note: standing up in a down clue makes the word read from bottom to top

parts.note: to miss a chance is to lose it

explanation.surface: A girl left miserable after being stood up by her boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman and 'stood up' like being jilted; they are a verb and a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person left bleak, abandoned and utterly wretched.

clue.text: Ball comes to rest on peg

parts.note: peg is informal for a leg
a break is a rest or pause

explanation.surface: A ball rolling to a halt against a peg, as in a game of bagatelle.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'rest on peg' puts the rest after the peg. A legbreak is a cricket delivery that turns from the leg side towards the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is a type of spin bowling delivery, so it names a single ball bowled.

clue.text: Highlight, ie streak, front part of hair

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of streak is kept

parts.note: the first letter of streak
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser explaining that a highlight is just a streak at the front of the hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Highlights and streaks belong together in a salon, which hides that 'Highlight' is the verb meaning emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight a point is to give it emphasis, which is what laying weight on it means.

clue.text: Flower-patterned cloth, carefully designed

parts.note: the Dee is a river, a thing that flows
plaid is a checked or tartan woollen fabric

explanation.surface: A length of fabric printed with a floral design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom, but in crosswords it is often a river, something that flows; the Dee runs through Scotland, Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan worked out thoroughly and secretly in advance is called this, especially a plot.

clue.text: Tax-related fine is set by State

parts.note: F is the pencil grading abbreviation for fine
taken as written
Cal is a short form for California

explanation.surface: A financial penalty for tax evasion imposed by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' sounds like the government imposing the fine; it is one American state, California.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes matters of public revenue and government finance, chiefly taxation.

clue.text: Girl comes up to town looking for a reference

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means rising, so the name is read from the bottom

parts.note: a girl's name
Reading is a town in Berkshire, west of London

explanation.surface: A girl travelling up to town to look for a job reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The reference is a grid reference on a map, not a testimonial.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpreting a map means hunting for grid references and locations on it.

clue.text: Board game with ten moves to counter

parts.note: a man is a counter in draughts or chess

indicators.note: pieces that move change position, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A board game with ten moves before you reach a counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Board, game, moves and counter all suggest draughts; 'to counter' places the shuffled letters after the piece. The board is the directors of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's board of directors is the body that runs it, its controlling executives collectively.

clue.text: Speculative by half — deposited in account after account

indicators.note: in a down clue, after places one part below the other

parts.note: AC is short for account

indicators.note: money deposited goes into an account, so one part goes inside

parts.note: AC is short for account
demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: A banker making a speculative deposit, splitting the money across two accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: The first account comes first, and the half sits within the second one.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretical, of no practical consequence: a question that is purely hypothetical is called this.

clue.text: Foul, bad, mean, grasping, low and abhorrent

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it inside
something foul is spoilt or corrupted, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
L marks low, as on a control dial

explanation.surface: A string of insults: foul, bad, mean, grasping, low and abhorrent.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a list of near-synonyms; only the first word, the last word and the middle ones are working.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserving of condemnation and hateful are both senses of the adjective, much as accursed is.

clue.text: Gearbox designed for transit causes it to break down

indicators.note: breaking down means falling to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist's transmission, built for a Ford Transit van, keeps making the van break down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gearbox' is read as a box for gear, your belongings, and transit as travelling; Transit is also a Ford van.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling case carries one's clothes and belongings, a container for gear on a journey.

clue.text: Girl in therapy for skin problem

indicators.note: a person in therapy is inside a course of treatment, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a cure is a course of treatment
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl undergoing treatment for a complaint of the skin, such as eczema.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'skin' is the surface layer of an old oil painting, not a person's.
explanation.definitionFit: The network of fine cracks in the varnish or paint of an old picture is a flaw in its outer surface.

clue.text: He puts his baby to bed before running off …

definitions.text: He puts his baby to bed before running off

parts.words: He puts his baby to bed before running off
parts.note: surface reading: a father settling his child for the night, then slipping out

parts.words: baby to bed before running off
parts.note: setter's reading: the baby is a newspaper, sent to bed (to press) before the presses run off copies

explanation.surface: A father puts his child to bed and then dashes off out.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, putting a paper to bed means finalising it for press, and running off means printing copies.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper signs it off for the presses each night.

clue.text: … to Fathers' Club

definitions.note: plural possessive, the answer is singular
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clergyman addressed as Father
second meaning: a small cudgel used by anglers to kill a caught fish

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the father runs off to his club.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis makes it look like the editor's evening out; the fishing club is the obscure sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic cleric is called Father, and anglers call their little weighted fish-killing cosh by the same name.

clue.text: Maenad danced about wearing a chaplet

indicators.note: dancing about means moving around in all directions, so the letters swap places

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A frenzied female worshipper of Bacchus dancing wildly with a wreath on her head.
explanation.walkthrough: A maenad was a wild follower of Dionysus, so a garland is perfectly at home in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a garland or wreath of flowers worn on the head.

clue.text: Present for appointment, having to hold on

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being on time for an appointment, and having to wait on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like an adjective meaning in attendance; it is a verb, to give.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something to a cause or charity is to give it as a gift.

clue.text: Duck a l'orange

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a colourful East Asian species of duck
second meaning: a small loose-skinned citrus fruit

explanation.surface: The classic French restaurant dish of roast duck in orange sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The dish name hides two separate meanings, one at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an ornamental Asian duck breed and a small easily peeled citrus fruit, the tangerine family.

clue.text: Old headdress vulgar — put on better

parts.note: the mob is the common people, the vulgar
to cap a story is to go one better than it

explanation.surface: Someone sneering that an old-fashioned headdress looks vulgar when worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar' as a noun once meant the common people, the mob; 'put on' sets the mob in front of the cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A large soft frilled bonnet worn indoors by women in the eighteenth century is this item.

clue.text: Crop tends to lie awkwardly

indicators.note: doing something awkwardly means doing it clumsily and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the first set of letters to be rearranged
the second set of letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A field crop that tends to lie flat in an awkward way after rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Lintseed is an old variant spelling of linseed.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed of flax, grown as a field crop for its oil, is what this word names.

clue.text: Fell, we hear, for this yarn

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: fell as an adjective means fierce or ruthless

explanation.surface: A tall story about a fell, a northern English hill, told as a yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a tale to go with 'we hear'; it is wool. Fell as an adjective means savage, as in 'one fell swoop'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thin worsted wool thread used for embroidery and tapestry work.

clue.text: Flower from a desert in bloom

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: geum is a garden flower, avens
to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: A flower that springs up when a desert bursts into bloom after rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like the sandy noun; it is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a genus of plants with fluffy blue or white heads, grown in borders as bedding.
